entities.name: Builds
entities.description: The five archetypes - Netrunner, Blade Dancer, Quake Brawler, Deadeye Gunslinger and Bolt Tech Specialist.
tips: Overclock Netrunner: Intelligence 20, Technical Ability 20, Body 20, Reflexes 9, Cool 12.
Deadeye Gunslinger rewards accurate aim - invest in Reflexes.
Bolt Tech Specialist fits charged shots through cover - invest in Technical Ability.
Quake Brawler and Blade Dancer survive mistakes thanks to finishers, Berserk and Adrenaline Rush.
Perks are refundable - you can switch between builds that share attributes.
Never lock attributes before testing a perk package at a lower level.

entities.name: Relics
entities.description: The Phantom Liberty skill tree. It upgrades cyberware with powerful passive bonuses.
tips: Relic perks come from the Phantom Liberty skill tree, not the main trees.
The first perk in each Relic branch costs 3 points, follow-ups cost 1.
Jailbreak unlocks new abilities for Arm cyberware.
Limiter Removal makes charged Gorilla Arms attacks knock down enemies.
Machine Learning makes destroying a Vulnerability grant crit damage - it stacks to 5.
Pick the Relic branch that matches the cyberware you actually run.

entities.name: Perks
entities.description: The five perk trees and how the points work.
tips: Each tree is split into branches and left and right paths.
The first perk in a branch costs 3 perk points, the follow-ups cost 1 each.
Intelligence is the Netrunner tree, Technical Ability is the tech/combat tree, Reflexes is the gunslinger tree, Body is the brawler tree, Cool is the stealth tree.
Update 2.1 retuned perks such as Spontaneous Obliteration and Die! Die! Die!.
Spend perk points on the branch you are committing to - mixing trees is expensive.

entities.name: Cyberware
entities.description: The implants you install. Each one takes capacity, and too many will cyberpsychose you.
tips: Capacity decides how many implants you can run - plan it like perks.
You start at 24 capacity and gain 3 per level, reaching 201 at level 60 before bonuses.
Renaissance Punk adds up to 20 capacity - 4 for each attribute at 9 or higher.
The Engineer skill adds 5 capacity at rank 10 and 10 at rank 30.
Edgerunner lets you go 50 over capacity, trading maximum health for extra slots.
Update 2.1 capped how many implants you can install - exceeding it causes cyberpsychosis.

entities.name: Cyberpsycho
entities.description: The condition caused by too much cyberware. It is a mechanic, not just a story.
tips: Overinstalling cyberware raises your cyberpsychosis level.
Update 2.1 restricted the implant count specifically to stop it.
As cyberpsychosis climbs, your max health drops and you can die from a seemingly small hit.
Spending money on thepsycho reduction at Nomad, or removing implants, lowers it.
David Martinez from Edgerunners is the extreme case - do not copy his implant count without accepting the penalty.

entities.name: Gangs
entities.description: The gangs of Night City and what each one wants.
tips: Each fixed-gang district has its own gang and its own jobs.
Completing a gang's jobs raises your standing and unlocks their gigs.
The gangs are the Maelstrom, 6th Street, Valentines, Animals, Voodoo Boys, Tyger Claws, 6th Street and the Handbrake crew groups.
All Foods, Trauma Team and assorted corpo jobs sit alongside the gang work.
Gang standing is per-district - do the jobs in the area you want to rank up in.

entities.name: Drops
entities.description: Legendary and epic gear - where it comes from and how to get it.
tips: Legendary weapons drop from specific bosses and cyberpsycho encounters.
The Relic unlocks new cyberware - including the Relic skill tree and some of the best gear.
Side gigs, gigs and cyberpsycho fights are the main legendary sources.
Iconic weapons are separate - they have fixed stats and unique names.
Do not sell epics you have not compared - the iconics drop into the same slot.

entities.name: Contracts
entities.description: The gig and job system that fills the map.
tips: Gigs are the small jobs - a fixed objective and a fixed payment.
Jobs are the larger multi-step contracts with better pay.
Both appear on the map with coloured markers - green for gigs, blue for jobs, purple for cyberpsycho missions.
Deliveries are the courier contracts - pay scales with distance and difficulty.
Complete gigs and jobs to build street cred, which opens the better contracts.
